entrypoints.summary: Creation of an issue comment containing /update-vrt on a pull request triggers the workflow; it resolves the pull request head owner, repository, and ref.
The disclosure specifies that an attacker can submit a pull request containing a replacement local setup action.

affected_components.role: Vulnerable comment-triggered privileged workflow that checks out PR content and invokes a local action.
Local composite-action definition demonstrating that the invoked action contains a Bash command-running step.

code_slices.fixed: The replacement generate workflow documents untrusted fork execution, uses contents: read, and produces artifacts; trusted apply logic validates that patches contain only PNG paths before git apply.
code_slices.surrounding_context: The original workflow is triggered by issue_comment creation when the comment contains /update-vrt and the issue is a pull request.
code_slices.vulnerable: The update-vrt job checks out repository and ref values obtained from the PR head, then runs uses: ./.github/actions/setup under contents and pull-requests write permissions.

negative_controls: No public workflow run log or preserved exploit execution result is supplied.
The patched untrusted generation workflow is declared contents: read and patch application rejects non-PNG paths.
observability.positive_marker: The workflow has the sequence of attacker-selected checkout followed by uses: ./.github/actions/setup while write permissions are declared.

preconditions: The attacker can open a pull request whose head repository/ref is selected by the workflow.
A qualifying /update-vrt issue comment triggers the workflow.
The attacker places a modified .github/actions/setup/action.yml in the pull-request tree.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A pull-request tree containing .github/actions/setup/action.yml with attacker-controlled command execution steps.
trigger_steps.summary: Submit a pull request with a substituted local composite-action definition, then cause the qualifying comment-triggered workflow to run against that PR head.

sources.concept: repository-local composite action resolved from checked-out content

impact.affected_asset: Actual repository contents and pull-request state.
impact.attacker_capability: Gain write access to repository contents and pull-request state through the workflow's contents: write and pull-requests: write permissions.
impact.security_effect: Execution of attacker-supplied commands in a repository-write-capable GitHub Actions job.

causal_trace.summary: A pull request head repository and ref selected by the comment-branch action are checked out by the comment-triggered job.

After checking out attacker-selected pull-request content, the job resolves and invokes the repository-local path ./.github/actions/setup while the job retains contents: write and pull-requests: write permissions.
The local setup action is a composite action containing a Bash run step; a substituted action definition in the checked-out tree can therefore supply commands executed by the workflow runner.

Runner execution of the substituted local action occurs in a workflow granted repository contents and pull-request write permissions, allowing the attacker to gain repository write access according to the disclosure.

failure.operation: GitHub Actions resolves and executes the composite action at ./.github/actions/setup after checkout of the PR head.

primary_invariant.statement: A privileged base-repository workflow must not execute a repository-local action resolved from an untrusted pull-request checkout.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The issue-comment workflow checks out the attacker-selected PR head and subsequently executes ./.github/actions/setup from that checkout while configured with write permissions.

quality.review_notes: The causal path is directly supported by immutable workflow and composite-action sources plus a coordinated disclosure. No preserved malicious PR, workflow execution log, or test run is present, so this record states a static workflow-semantics oracle rather than an observed exploit result. The related GHSL-2024-326 branch-name shell-interpolation issue is intentionally excluded.

remediation.invariant_restored: The final design runs the attacker-checkout and local setup action only in a pull_request generate workflow with contents: read, then permits the trusted application workflow to apply only patches whose changed paths are PNG files and stages only PNGs.
mitigation_classes: separate untrusted generation from trusted application
least-privilege permissions for untrusted pull-request execution
validate generated patch file paths before trusted application

oracle.channel: workflow source and remediation patch review
oracle.expected_negative: The patched generate workflow declares contents: read for the untrusted checkout, and the apply logic rejects patches containing non-PNG paths before applying them.
oracle.expected_positive: The vulnerable workflow statically exhibits attacker-selected checkout followed by local-action invocation in a job with write permissions.
